To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the weak lensing contribution of filaments in the context of the relativistic MOND/TeVes is not negligible, (ii) this contribution can be of either sign, (iii) this effect is not limited to the region around the filament but can be observed at any point in the sky, and (iv) this effect is likely to be of a complex nature and can be used to falsifiy MOND/TeVEs.
the weak lensing effect due to a filament is (1) much larger than in GR and (2) can occur even when there is no projected mass along the line of sight.

(1) the weak lensing effect of intercluster filaments can be substantial in the context of relativistically modified gravity, and (2) it is likely to be a source of systematic error when interpreting weak lensing signals of systems embedded in or projected on filaments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gravitational lensing signal of intercluster filaments in the context of general relativity and MOND.
the question of whether the weak gravitational lensing signal of a single intercluster filament is negligible in the context of GR or not, as is commonly assumed.
the gravitational effects of the intergalactic filamentary structure.

MOND is falsified, but only in the context of a specific implementation of the theory.
weak lensing by filaments is negligible in GR, but can be significant in TeVeS and its variants.
weak lensing is an extremely useful tool to test MOND, but that the interpretation of the results is complicated by filamentary structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the context of the Bekenstein MOND theory, the weak lensing signals from filaments and the intergalactic medium are not negligible.
the weak lensing effect of the intercluster filaments is negligible in GR but not necessarily in MOND.
the weak lensing signals in MOND/TeVes are more complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to fully understand weak lensing signals of galaxy clusters, one needs to take into account the effects of intercluster filaments, and this is true for all theories of gravity.
the weak lensing signals in MOND/TeVes are more complicated than those in the standard ΛCDM model, and the weak lensing maps should be interpreted with caution.
in the context of relativistically modified gravity, gravitational lensing by filaments cannot be ignored.
